# The claim ledger

Every factual claim every lesson makes, with the evidence for it. Written against `llvmorg-23.1.0`.

`observed` means somebody ran it, on two platforms. `cited` means it is in the LLVM source or its documentation at the pinned tag, at the line given. `inferred` means neither, and a lesson is allowed at most three.

70 claims: 43 observed, 26 cited, 1 inferred.

## t02_first_look_at_the_ir

| Claim | Confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A module's top level is target description lines, globals, functions with bodies, functions without, then attribute groups and metadata. @ starts a global, % something local to a function, ! metadata. | observed | cell whole_module<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, same set of kinds on both |
| A basic block is a label, then instructions, then exactly one terminator, which is the last instruction. A block with no terminator or with a terminator in the middle is not accepted. | cited | cell inside_a_function<br>llvm/docs/LangRef.md:1038-1043 and 9968-9971@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| The pointer type is ptr and carries no pointee type. Four C functions taking int *, char *, a pointer to a 128 byte struct and a function pointer all compile to the identical LLVM signature ptr (ptr). | observed | cell four_pointers<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, four identical signatures on both, and llvm/docs/LangRef.md:4713-4718@llvmorg-23.1.0, whose whole Pointer Type section describes address spaces and representation width and never mentions a pointee |
| The old typed pointer syntax i32* still parses. The parser translates it to ptr and the i32 is gone from what LLVM stores, so material written before the change does not visibly break. | observed | cell old_syntax<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, both print back ptr |
| Typed pointers forced the front end to emit no-op bitcasts purely to satisfy the type system, cost memory and compile time, and made passes miss optimisations when they failed to look through one. Removing the pointee type removed that whole category. | cited | cell old_syntax, and the prose that follows it<br>llvm/docs/OpaquePointers.rst:78-90@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| Changing a load through an int * argument from i32 to i64, and changing nothing else but the return type, produces IR the verifier accepts, because no record of the C pointee type survives in the file. | observed | cell nothing_checks_it<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, verifier exits 0 on both |
| The type on a getelementptr supplies a stride rather than describing memory. The same C array index is emitted over i32 at -O0 and over [4 x i8] at -O1, both striding four bytes per index to the same address. | observed | cell gep_is_arithmetic<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, i32 at -O0 and [4 x i8] at -O1 on both |
| Unnamed register numbers are not stored. SlotTracker::processFunction walks one counter over unnamed arguments, then for each block the block itself if unnamed, then each unnamed instruction whose type is not void, and the printer uses the result. | cited | cells who_names_the_registers and void_takes_nothing<br>llvm/lib/IR/AsmWriter.cpp:1143-1166@llvmorg-23.1.0, CreateFunctionSlot at 1408-1417 |
| Adding the label entry: to the entry block changes every number in the function, because an unnamed block consumes a slot and a named one does not. | The parser accepts any unnamed value number at least as large as the one it expects and renumbers on output, so %5 and %99 and %4 are all accepted, and a number that is too small is an error reading "instruction expected to be numbered '%N' or greater". | cited | cells who_names_the_registers, void_takes_nothing and the_error<br>llvm/lib/AsmParser/LLParser.cpp:3595-3601, LLParser::checkValueID@llvmorg-23.1.0, message reproduced on both platforms |

## t03_reading_ll

| Claim | Confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Every block label in clang's output carries a generated "; preds =" comment listing the blocks that can branch to it, and a loop header is a block with a predecessor that appears below it. | observed | cell the_loop_at_o0<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, for.cond lists for.inc and entry on both |
| Control flow at this level is only blocks and two shapes of br, an unconditional br label and a conditional br i1 that takes a one bit condition and two labels, true first. | cited | cell the_loop_at_o0<br>llvm/docs/LangRef.md, the br instruction@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| SSA constrains registers and not memory. A stack slot may be stored to any number of times, which is how clang emits a loop that assigns total on every iteration while every register in the function is assigned once. | observed | cell the_loop_at_o0<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, three allocas and eight load or store instructions and no phi at -O0 on both |
| Running mem2reg alone on the -O0 loop removes all three allocas and the eight load and store instructions and produces two phi instructions at the top of the loop header, leaving the five blocks and the branches between them unchanged. | observed | cell mem2reg<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, identical output on both apart from dso_local |
| A phi is a list of value and label pairs, one for each predecessor of its block, and the value it takes is the one paired with the block control arrived from. | cited | cell mem2reg<br>llvm/docs/LangRef.md:13370-13372@llvmorg-23.1.0, "the phi instruction logically takes on the value specified by the pair corresponding to the predecessor basic block that executed" immediately before the current one |
| A swap inside a loop compiles, after mem2reg, to two phi instructions in the same block each of which names the other, and the first of them names a value defined on the line below it. | observed | cell the_swap<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, the same two lines in the same order on both |
| Executing that IR with lli gives 20, 10 and 20 for one, two and three iterations, so the pair really alternates. Reading the two phis as assignments in order predicts 10 for every count above one. | observed | cell run_it<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, exit codes 20, 10, 20 on both |
| The phis in a block all take effect together on the edge into the block, and each reads its incoming value as it was in the predecessor. LangRef puts the use of each incoming value on the edge from the predecessor rather than at the point in the block where the phi appears. | cited | cells the_swap and run_it<br>llvm/docs/LangRef.md:13358-13361@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| Because a phi's use of an incoming value happens on the edge rather than inside the block, a phi may name a value defined below it, while an ordinary instruction that does the same is rejected with "Instruction does not dominate all uses!". | cited | cells the_swap and the_two_rules<br>llvm/lib/IR/Verifier.cpp:5211@llvmorg-23.1.0, message reproduced on both platforms |
| A phi may not have an ordinary instruction above it in its block. The verifier rejects that with "PHI nodes not grouped at top of basic block!", and the rule is what makes the dominance exemption well defined. | cited | cell the_two_rules<br>llvm/lib/IR/Verifier.cpp:3804@llvmorg-23.1.0 and llvm/docs/LangRef.md:13354-13356@llvmorg-23.1.0, "There must be no non-phi instructions between the start of a basic block and the PHI instructions", message reproduced on both platforms |

## t05_the_pipeline_string

| Claim | Confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| sroa,indvars,loop-deletion leaves sum_to with the entry block and for.end and no loop, while sroa,loop-deletion,indvars leaves all five blocks and the loop intact. Neither is an error. | observed | cell same_names_new_order<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, 9 instructions in 2 blocks against 12 in 5 on both |
| loop-deletion eliminates loops with a computable trip count that have no side effects and do not contribute to the return value, so the loop in sum_to is not dead until indvars has rewritten what comes after it. Running loop-deletion first therefore wastes it, and a pipeline entry runs once with no second chance. | cited | cell same_names_new_order<br>llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopDeletion.cpp:9-12@llvmorg-23.1.0, "eliminating loops with non-infinite computable trip counts that have no side effects or volatile instructions, and do not contribute to the computation of the function's return value" |
| opt reads the first name in a -passes list, decides which level that pass belongs to, and wraps the whole list at that level, so loop-deletion,indvars,sroa is parsed as a loop pipeline and fails with "unknown loop pass 'sroa'". | cited | cells the_order_that_will_not_parse and where_a_pass_lives<br>llvm/lib/Passes/PassBuilder.cpp:2715-2719@llvmorg-23.1.0, "If the first name isn't at the module layer, wrap the pipeline up automatically", and llvm/docs/NewPassManager.md:449-457@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| The message is produced by the pipeline parser rather than by any pass, and there is one per level, so the wording tells you which level opt had settled on. | cited | cell where_a_pass_lives<br>llvm/lib/Passes/PassBuilder.cpp:2553@llvmorg-23.1.0 for the loop wording and llvm/lib/Passes/PassBuilder.cpp:2486@llvmorg-23.1.0 for the function wording |
| The levels nest as module, then optionally call graph component, then function, then loop. A list may go from a wider level to a narrower one and never back, which is why globaldce,instcombine runs and instcombine,globaldce does not. | cited | cell where_a_pass_lives<br>llvm/docs/NewPassManager.md:445@llvmorg-23.1.0, "The nesting is: module (-> cgscc) -> function -> loop, where the CGSCC nesting is optional" |
| A narrower pass named in a wider list is wrapped in an adaptor, and each name gets its own, so globaldce,instcombine,loop-deletion becomes globaldce, then function(instcombine), then a separate function(loop(loop-deletion)). | cited | cell print_the_pipeline<br>llvm/docs/NewPassManager.md:459-465@llvmorg-23.1.0 and llvm/lib/Passes/PassBuilder.cpp:2173@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| Two adaptors mean two walks over the functions of the module, and one pass manager holding both passes means one walk that runs both on each function. Upstream recommends the grouped form for cache locality and says it can change the quality of the optimisation. | cited | cell print_the_pipeline<br>llvm/docs/NewPassManager.md:112-140@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| The pipeline opt builds from -passes=sroa is function(sroa<modify-cfg>),verify, so the printed form shows the adaptor, the pass parameters filled in with their defaults, and a verify run that opt appends. | observed | cell print_the_pipeline<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, byte identical on both |
| default<O2> prints as a single pipeline text of about 4800 characters. The exact length and entry count are target dependent, 4791 characters and 120 entries on macOS arm64 and 4770 and 119 on Linux x86_64, which is why the lesson prints them rather than stating them. | observed | cell the_o2_string<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0 |
| Feeding the printed default<O2> text back to -passes= produces byte identical IR to running default<O2> by name, and opt checks this itself by building a pipeline from the text before printing it. | cited | cell feed_it_back<br>llvm/tools/opt/NewPMDriver.cpp:171-176@llvmorg-23.1.0, the -disable-pipeline-verification flag whose description is that it "Disables verifying that the textual pipeline generated by -print-pipeline-passes can be used to create a pipeline" |
| simplifycfg appears eight times in default<O2> with five distinct sets of options. Seven of the eight are given keep-loops, three are given switch-to-arithmetic, and exactly one, the seventh, is given switch-to-lookup. | observed | cell eight_simplifycfgs<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, the same eight instances in the same positions on both |
| On a six case switch, simplifycfg<no-switch-to-lookup> leaves the switch and its arms, and simplifycfg<switch-to-lookup> produces a private constant array named @switch.table.pick and a function that is a range check and a load. | observed | cell one_option_one_table<br>measured on macOS arm64 LLVM 23.1.0 and Linux x86_64 LLVM 23.1.0, 23 instructions and no global against 11 and one on both |

## x03_your_first_fold

| Claim | Confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| At -O1 clang turns `a > 0 && b > 0` into a single `and i1` and leaves `a > 0 && (a << b) > 5` as a `select i1`. | observed | cell two_shapes<br>llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineSelect.cpp:3754-3806@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| A shift whose count is equal to or larger than the width of the value being shifted produces poison, which is why %sh in this lesson can be poison. | cited | cell check<br>llvm/docs/LangRef.md:11170-11173@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| Replacing `select i1 %ok, i1 %big, i1 false` with `and i1 %ok, %big` is not a valid refinement, and Alive2 gives a = 0, b = 32 as the input that breaks it. | observed | cell check<br> |
| The original and the naive fold print the same answer for every one of the six test inputs, including the counterexample a = 0, b = 32, because poison is not a value lli can produce or observe. | observed | cell tests<br> |
| The and version can be replaced by the select version and Alive2 verifies it, which is the same pair of files that failed in the other direction. | observed | cell backwards<br> |
| Freezing the true arm before the `and` makes the fold verify, in under a tenth of a second. | observed | cell check2<br>llvm/docs/LangRef.md:13436@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| InstCombine performs both this fold and its `or` mirror only when impliesPoisonOrCond proves the arm cannot be poison, and the comment above the pair says so in as many words. | cited | cell instcombine<br>llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineSelect.cpp:3754-3806@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| Swapping the `shl` for an `add` with no nsw makes real instcombine perform the fold, and putting the `shl` back makes it decline again. | observed | cell instcombine<br> |
| Alive2 finds the counterexample for the wrong sdiv fold at every width in hundredths of a second, and proving the correct version cliffs between i8, which it does in about 0.04s, and i32, where it exhausts a five second budget. | observed | cell bound, and docs/probes/alive.md for the wider sweep<br> |
| A timeout is a fourth answer alongside correct, wrong and error, and it means nothing was proved in either direction. | observed | cell bound<br>toolkit/irx/verify.py and toolkit/tests/test_verify.py |
| The pass plugin header is llvm/Plugins/PassPlugin.h in LLVM 23, not llvm/Passes/PassPlugin.h. | observed | cell plugin<br>llvm/include/llvm/Plugins/PassPlugin.h@llvmorg-23.1.0 |
| Both plugins in this lesson are loaded into one opt process, and without an anonymous namespace the second pass class resolves to the first one's symbols and silently runs the wrong code. | observed | measured on macOS arm64 while writing this lesson, which is how the bug was found<br> |
| Each %%irxplug cell compiles and loads in under two seconds, well inside the twenty second budget the lesson was designed against. | observed | cell plugin, cell plugin2<br> |
